summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat printed Tom Allen's card disputing Ben Hogan's claim to be champion of America, offering to back Jack Madden against Hogan for $1,000 a side or to fight Hogan himself in Canada at odds of $5,000 to $1,000.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Saturday, November 29, 1873'; masthead 'Daily Democrat'. Pre-1875 merger. Allen's letter is addressed 'To the Editor of the Democrat'.

facts.fact: Allen offered to match Jack Madden to fight Ben Hogan within ten weeks for $1,000 a side, in Canada within fifty miles of Detroit

Allen challenged Hogan to fight him anywhere in Canada at two days' to ten weeks' notice, staking $5,000 to $1,000, with no more than five friends each, and offered to bet $1,000 he would not get a black eye
Allen disputed Hogan's claim to be champion of America after the broken-up fight
facts.quote: No man can be champion of America without fighting for and winning that title, and most assuredly the title cannot be claimed by a man who gives all his portion of the stake money to a gang of murderers, who not only broke up the fight, but threatened to kill me and my friends.

facts.fact: Allen put up $3,000 in greenbacks as collateral for the Illinois bail bond that freed Arthur Chambers
